relations.note: Taû fathers Mbói Tu'i with Kerana.
Kerana bears Mbói Tu'i as her second monstrous son.
Arasy's prenatal curse condemns Taû's offspring to monstrous forms.
Teju Jagua is Mbói Tu'i's first-born brother.

relations.myth: Porãsy and the cave of the monsters
relations.note: They gather, cry out, and perish together in the burning cave.
Moñái is Mbói Tu'i's third-born brother.

relations.myth: Porãsy and the cave of the monsters
relations.note: Moñái convenes the brothers for his supposed wedding; all perish.
Jasy Jatere is one of Mbói Tu'i's six brothers.

relations.myth: Porãsy and the cave of the monsters
relations.note: They attend the cave gathering and perish together in the fire.
Kurupi is one of Mbói Tu'i's six brothers.

relations.myth: Porãsy and the cave of the monsters
relations.note: They attend the cave gathering and perish together in the fire.
Ao-Ao is one of Mbói Tu'i's six brothers.

relations.myth: Porãsy and the cave of the monsters

Luisón is one of Mbói Tu'i's six brothers.

relations.myth: Porãsy and the cave of the monsters
relations.note: They attend the cave gathering and perish together in the fire.

relations.myth: Porãsy and the cave of the monsters
relations.note: Porãsy lures Mbói Tu'i and his brothers into a wedding trap.

relations.myth: Porãsy and the cave of the monsters
relations.note: Porãsy sacrifices herself and dies in the cave with Mbói Tu'i.

relations.myth: Porãsy and the cave of the monsters
relations.note: Tumê seals and burns the cave, killing Mbói Tu'i and the others.
Rupavê curses Mbói Tu'i for revealing the guarded secret path.
Rupavê transforms the parrot into a wingless serpent-parrot.
